title: Round 21 Northern Rockies state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Montana and Wyoming. Every seeded row reproduces one accepted USGS GNIS Geocoder candidate screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point. Granite Peak and Jackson Lake also carry GNIS Domestic Names per-ID checks.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Political divisions, counties, springs, canals, ranges, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Per-ID identity checks for Granite Peak (784178), where three same-name Summit records were returned, and Jackson Lake (1609177), where the per-ID detail identifies Class=Reservoir in Teton County rather than the same-name Natrona County lake record.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake or Reservoir according to the official feature kind confirmed per ID where records are ambiguous, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

montana.title: Montana statewide frame

identityDecisions.candidate: Granite Peak, Montana: Summit records 784178 (Park County), 784179 (Madison County), and 784177 (Park County)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded 784178 after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Summit, Primary State=Montana, Primary County=Park County, and coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point marked High Point on the Crazy Peak map; coordinate matches the Geocoder exactly.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The Madison County Summit record (784179) and the second Park County Summit record (784177) are different features and are not verified by this row.

identityDecisions.candidate: Lake McDonald, Montana: Lake 787038 and populated place 785919
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The lake primary point is not the settlement point, shoreline, or lake-area centroid.

identityDecisions.candidate: Yellowstone River and Missouri River under states=MT
identityDecisions.decision: No gazetteer rows seeded; generalized context corridors only.
identityDecisions.reason: Both exact-name state-filtered Geocoder screens returned empty arrays.

The screen returned only Glacier National Park Division records (FEATURE_IDs 1940629 and 1940630), not a park feature record; archived Park classes are likewise absent from the current Geocoder surface, as previously recorded for California.

identityDecisions.candidate: Bighorn River: Montana screen returned Yellowstone County Stream 779903; Wyoming screen returned an empty array
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The Montana primary point does not verify the Wyoming reach of the same-named river; no Wyoming Bighorn River row is claimed.

identityDecisions.candidate: North Platte River, Snake River, and the Green River main stem under states=WY
identityDecisions.decision: No gazetteer rows seeded; generalized context corridors only where shown.
identityDecisions.reason: The North Platte screen returned an empty array; the Snake River screen returned only the Snake River Mountain Ranges record; the Green River screen returned town/division/canal records plus a different same-name Weston County Stream record (1600086), not the main-stem river.

identityDecisions.candidate: Jackson Lake, Wyoming: Teton County 1609177 and Natrona County 1590031
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded 1609177 as a Reservoir row after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Reservoir, Primary County=Teton County, and coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point (variant name Jackson Lake Reservoir).
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The Natrona County same-name lake record (1590031) is a different feature and is not verified by this row; the stored point is not a shoreline or dam structure.

identityDecisions.candidate: Devils Tower: Summit 1609083 and populated place 1604684
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The summit primary point does not verify the settlement.

identityDecisions.candidate: Grand Teton: Summit 1609199 and Grand Teton Canal 1589026
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The summit primary point is not the canal record or a peak-area polygon.

identityDecisions.candidate: Rock Springs: populated place 1593588 versus Springs records 1593589 and 1593590
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The town point does not verify either spring.

identityDecisions.reason: The screen returned a populated place, reservation/division records, two canals, a Hot Springs County Stream record, a Teton County lake, and a mountain range under the same name; the 12-row starter composition does not require resolving that pile, and no per-ID statewide-river identity was established in this round.

knownLimitations: Montana and Wyoming are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence, and the returned county is primary-county provenance. Granite Peak and Jackson Lake additionally carry per-ID Domestic Names detail checks.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include small areas outside their state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
